The pytest closure operator ensures that only relevant test files are considered, forming a Boolean algebra under inclusion. The mock validation kernel identifies adversarial leakage by checking whether all dependencies are mocked, which introduces a failure mode when live calls occur. Syntax integrity checks act as a filter ensuring that only valid code enters the system. These primitives form a layered logical structure where each layer enforces a constraint on the next, creating a robust verification pipeline. The failure modes arise from violations of these constraints—specifically, network leakage in tests and syntax errors in code. The duality lies in the fact that both test isolation and code integrity must hold simultaneously for a system to be considered valid.
